coding.display: ST elevation (STEMI) myocardial infarction of anterior wall
Percutaneous transcatheter placement of intracoronary stent

attachment.data:
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
Patient is a 69-year-old male who presented to the emergency department on 2024-10-20 at 08:14 with acute onset chest pain radiating to left arm, diaphoresis, and shortness of breath. ECG on arrival showed ST elevation in leads V1-V4 consistent with anterior STEMI.

PROCEDURES:
The patient was taken emergently to the cardiac catheterization laboratory. Door-to-balloon time was 72 minutes. Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) was performed at 09:26 with placement of drug-eluting stent in the proximal LAD. TIMI 3 flow restored.

DISCHARGE SUMMARY:
Patient tolerated procedure well. EF on echo 45%. Discharged on dual antiplatelet therapy, statin, beta-blocker, and ACE inhibitor. Follow-up with cardiology in 2 weeks.
